patchHistoryNotes.note: Valve: CS2 sprays tuned to match CS:GO 128-tick size (slightly smaller than 64-tick).
Valve patch note: 'Adjusted camera motion due to recoil to match CS:GO more closely. Bullet trajectories should continue to match CS2.' (camera/view punch only)
Third-party patch timelines report no AK-47 bullet-trajectory change since launch (only MP9 recoil changed, 2025-07). Not verified against Valve's own notes line by line.

units.angles: degrees of view angle; x = yaw (+ right), y = pitch (+ up = bullets climbing). Compensation = mouse direction opposite to the bullet offset.
units.vdataRecoilFields: m_flRecoilMagnitude / m_flRecoilAngle(Variance) are engine-internal impulse parameters, NOT degrees of final crosshair offset; they cannot be turned into a per-bullet trajectory without Valve's (unpublished) table generation + punch decay model.

shotTimes_s.formula: t_k = (k-1) * 0.1, k=1..30 (continuous; CS2 sub-tick fires at the real cycle time, do not quantize to 64/128 tick)
shotTimes_s.note: timing model per sub-tick discussion; see https://www.reddit.com/r/GlobalOffensive/comments/16ithxo/

recovery.note: Recovery time of accumulated inaccuracy/recoil, interpolated between initial and final values across the transition bullets. Exact decay curve not published by Valve.

accuracy.note: Random spread is ADDED on top of the deterministic pattern in game; a trainer should show it as a tolerance ring, not as part of the ideal path. Units are engine-internal (radians-like), conversion not officially documented.

validationTargets.caveat: Aggregate envelope only (no per-bullet data published; per-bullet plots on that page are images). Measured 2023; use as sanity check that a measured 30-shot pattern spans ~11.06° vertically and ~7.14° horizontally.

perBullet.status: EMPTY — not obtainable from an allowed source

schema.x_deg: cumulative yaw offset of bullet impact vs. aim point (+right)

compensation.status: EMPTY — derive after perBullet is measured
compensation.rule: comp_k = (-x_deg_k, -y_deg_k): the cumulative view-angle movement the player must apply by shot k. Mouse right = +x, mouse pulled down = -y in view terms.

notes: 0.022 = CS2 default m_yaw/m_pitch (deg per mouse count at sensitivity 1), same as CS:GO; CS2 always uses raw input (m_rawinput removed).
Example: 11.06 deg vertical at sens 1.0 / 800 DPI -> 11.06/(0.022)/800*2.54 = 1.596 cm (arithmetic only).

measurementProcedure: Offline local server only (Practice / 'map de_dust2' with bots off), never on official/community servers.

Console: sv_cheats 1; bot_kick; sv_infinite_ammo 1; weapon_accuracy_nospread 1 (removes random spread, leaves deterministic recoil); sv_showimpacts 1; sv_showimpacts_time 10; cl_showpos 1; host_timescale 0.1 (optional, for readable capture). All these convars exist in DumpSource2/convars.txt of the same snapshot.

Stand still, aim at a flat wall at a known distance, fire one full 30-round magazine WITHOUT touching the mouse (fire via keyboard bind so no hand input contaminates the result). Record with high-fps lossless capture.

Extract the 30 impact markers (sv_showimpacts boxes) from the screenshot/frames; convert screen px -> degrees with CS2 FOV model (fov 90 horizontal at 4:3, Hor+ ~106.26 deg at 16:9): deg = atan(px_offset / (0.5*screenWidth / tan(hfov/2))) in each axis.
Repeat >=5 magazines, average per bullet, verify std-dev small (pattern is deterministic once nospread=1), and check envelope against validationTargets (~11.06 deg high, ~7.14 deg wide).
Record the game build number with the dataset; re-measure after any patch that mentions recoil.

rejectedCandidates.reason: Obtained its 30-point AK array from the page's public JS bundle. Every step has length exactly 30.0 and direction within ±70° — i.e. it is a plain cumulative sum of the raw vdata impulse parameters (magnitude 30, angle variance 70) with no smoothing / view-punch decay / scaling. Result keeps climbing linearly for all 30 shots (height:width ≈ 8.2:1) vs csstats measured 11.06°:7.14° (≈1.55:1). Not a valid in-game trajectory; also no license. Not included.
Its own page states pattern data comes from an RCS (recoil-compensation) project — excluded by policy.
Repos with per-bullet AK tables found earlier were macro/RCS-derived or based on reverse-engineered game binaries — excluded by policy.
